text: The tide remembers you. Ask, if you must.

choices.label: Tell me about the world beyond.

text: You've been out there. I can hear the sea on you. Did the city move while you watched it?

choices.label: Tell me about the world beyond.

text: This island is drowned stone that floats. Don't ask me how; the sea keeps its own secrets.
I fish, I watch the water, and I talk to it. Sometimes it answers.
A world of endless water. One last city lies drowned out there, and it doesn't stay in one place for long.
The deep keeps its own monsters. Patience and lungs matter more than speed.
Nobody knows for certain. There is only the old saying:
“The sea lets no one pass while the old guardian keeps watch in his drowned halls.”
Make of it what you will. I've said too much already.
The city's treasures are many small pieces that add up to something whole. Hoard what you find; don't waste it.
Bring more air than you think you need. Then bring more.
